lessons.title: The short-u hook returns at R4
lessons.gloss: retrieve the short-u sign at its fourth spacing window

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say short u once. Picture its small hook below a consonant before you look at any form.

Read ુ ી (short-u sign — long-ii sign) ુ once and score recognition 3/3. The short-u sign introduced at position 30 has now travelled 61 lessons to position 91: this closes its R4 window. Repair only a missed sign.

segments.prompt: Read this shuffled sign row aloud: ુ ી (short-u sign — long-ii sign) ુ.
acceptedResponses: short-u sign; long-ii sign; short-u sign

feedback.correct: You kept the below-letter short-u hook distinct from long ii.
feedback.incorrect: Compare only the missed sign, cover the names, and read the row once more.

segments.text: Keep the visible row covered. Write the three sound cues, then score writing 3/3 separately. A perfect reading score cannot replace the written one.

segments.prompt: Cover every model. Write: long-ii sign, short-u sign, short-u sign.

feedback.correct: The short-u hook returned twice from sound with no model.
feedback.incorrect: Check only a missed sign, cover the model again, and rewrite that cue.

segments.text: Where does ુ sit? (Below its consonant.)

lessons.title: The name exchange returns after a long interval
lessons.headword: મારું નામ … છે। તમારું નામ શું છે?
lessons.romanization: mārũ nām … chhe. tamārũ nām shũ chhe?
lessons.gloss: retrieve the introduction exchange after a long interval

notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: With the page covered, say the three pieces for my name is: mārũ — nām — chhe.

Read the three lines once and score meaning retrieval 3/3. Position 35 was already a zero-atom checkpoint, so position 96 uses the open slot to close R3 name-exchange debt rather than pretending to retrieve a nonexistent new atom.

segments.prompt: Read the shuffled lines and give each meaning: તમને મળીને આનંદ થયો. / તમારું નામ શું છે? / મારું નામ મીરા છે.
acceptedResponses: pleased to meet you. / what is your name? / my name is mira.

feedback.correct: All three introduction lines returned in a new order.
feedback.incorrect: Check only the missed line, cover its meaning, and read the three lines again.

segments.text: Cover every Gujarati model and write the three English-cued lines. Score written production 3/3 separately from reading; repair only a missed line.

segments.prompt: Cover every Gujarati model. Write: My name is Arun. / What is your name? / Pleased to meet you.
acceptedResponses: મારું નામ અરુણ છે। / તમારું નામ શું છે? / તમને મળીને આનંદ થયો।

feedback.correct: You produced the complete introduction from meaning with no model.
feedback.incorrect: Check only the missed line, cover it, and produce that line once more from its English cue.

segments.text: Which you belongs in this polite exchange? (tame.)
